name: King of Arad
overview: The King of Arad was a male ruler who opposed the Israelites during their journey in the wilderness at the time of the Exodus. He engaged in battle against Israel and captured some of the Israelites, demonstrating hostility toward God's people during this formative period.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Arad' simply denotes his position as the ruler of the city or region of Arad. The name means 'king of Arad' and is a descriptive title rather than a personal name, reflecting his royal authority rather than a divine designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for the King of Arad beyond his role as a hostile ruler who fought against Israel. There are no known familial ties or descendants mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Arad is significant in the biblical narrative as an early adversary of Israel during their wilderness wanderings. His opposition and capture of Israelites underscore the challenges and conflicts faced by God's people as they moved toward the Promised Land. His actions highlight the spiritual and physical opposition encountered during the Exodus period.
